name: Sheba son of Bichri
charge: Insurrection: we have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse
summary: After Absalom’s revolt, while the men of Israel and the men of Judah quarrelled over who had the right to bring the king home, Sheba the son of Bichri, a Benjamite and a man of Belial, blew a trumpet, declared that Israel had no part in David, and drew the men of Israel away after him (2 Samuel 19:41-43; 2 Samuel 20:1-2). Joab pursued him to Abel of Beth-maachah and laid siege to the city. A wise woman of Abel spoke with Joab, and the people of the city delivered Sheba’s head over the wall, so that one rebel died and the city was spared (2 Samuel 20:14-22).
offenseFull: The quarrel came first. When the tribes debated bringing David back, the men of Judah claimed the king as their near kin, the men of Israel claimed ten parts in him and more right in David, and the words of Judah were the fiercer (2 Samuel 19:41-43). The study notes mark this as the tribal strife that would later split the northern and southern kingdoms, though they were all Israel. Into that quarrel stepped Sheba the son of Bichri, a Benjamite. Scripture calls him a man of Belial, and the notes say plainly what that means: a devil. He blew a trumpet, declared that they had no part in David and no inheritance in the son of Jesse, and sent every man of Israel to his tents. The men of Israel went up from following David to follow Sheba, while the men of Judah held to their king from Jordan to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 20:1-2).

A quarrel between brethren became a banner of rebellion against the king the Lord had set over them, and David weighed it at once. He told Abishai that Sheba would now do them more harm than Absalom had done, and sent him out with Joab’s men, the Cherethites, the Pelethites and all the mighty men, to pursue Sheba before he could reach fenced cities and escape (2 Samuel 20:6-7). On the road Joab murdered Amasa, the man David had named captain in his place, taking him by the beard as if to kiss him and striking him with a sword he had fastened out of sight; the notes call Joab grimy and shady (2 Samuel 20:8-10). The pursuit went on through all the tribes to Abel of Beth-maachah, where Sheba shut himself in. Joab’s army cast up a bank against the city and battered the wall to throw it down (2 Samuel 20:14-15). One man’s rebellion had put a whole city of Israel under siege.
judgmentFull: The end came through a woman. A wise woman called from the wall and asked that Joab come near so she could speak with him. The teaching on this passage draws out her manner. She had enough respect to come to the leader who was bringing the harm on the city and ask him for a hearing. She made sure she knew who he was, which showed that she recognised his authority. She asked him to hear his handmaid, humbling herself and speaking respectfully, not loud and not up in his space. She reminded him of the old saying that men would ask counsel at Abel and so settle a matter. She told him she was one of the peaceable and faithful in Israel, so that he knew her character and her good reputation among her people. Only then did she ask why he would destroy a city that was a mother in Israel and swallow up the inheritance of the Lord (2 Samuel 20:16-19). A man in the heat of war wants to take the head, so she calmed him first and spoke to him reasonably and peaceably.

Joab answered that he had no wish to destroy. His matter was with one man of mount Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri, who had lifted up his hand against King David; if the city delivered him alone, Joab would leave. She promised that Sheba’s head would be thrown over the wall, went to all the people in her wisdom, and they cut off his head and threw it out to Joab (2 Samuel 20:20-22). She negotiated with the captain and stopped the onslaught on the city. The sentence fell on the rebel alone. Joab blew the trumpet, the army withdrew from the city every man to his tent, and Joab returned to the king at Jerusalem (2 Samuel 20:22). Sheba had used a trumpet to scatter Israel from David, and a trumpet ended his revolt. Joab stayed over all the host of Israel, and David’s officers stood in their places again (2 Samuel 20:23-26).

The teaching carries the lesson into the house of Israel today. The Most High puts that kind of spirit on sisters who know how to speak to men and become peacemakers, and a man who is supposed to have wisdom should be able to recognise it rather than bring down a whole house because of one loud mouth. That is why wise women are lifted up and honoured among the people and not kept beneath: the people know the history of their foremothers, and there are sisters with gifts that can do what the brothers cannot.

taught.title: 2 Samuel 19: The King Returns to His House

lawsResolved.text: Rebellion and insurrection against the government is punishable by death.
Whoever rebels against the laws of the land shall be put to death.
We should not rebel or cause insurrection against the established government.

text.text: And, behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said unto the king, Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away, and have brought the king, and his household, and all David’s men with him, over Jordan?

And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the king is near of kin to us: wherefore then be ye angry for this matter? have we eaten at all of the king’s cost? or hath he given us any gift?

And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more right in David than ye: why then did ye despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king? And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.

And there happened to be there a man of Belial, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he blew a trumpet, and said, We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, O Israel.
So every man of Israel went up from after David, and followed Sheba the son of Bichri: but the men of Judah clave unto their king, from Jordan even to Jerusalem.
And he went through all the tribes of Israel unto Abel, and to Beth–maachah, and all the Berites: and they were gathered together, and went also after him.

And they came and besieged him in Abel of Beth–maachah, and they cast up a bank against the city, and it stood in the trench: and all the people that were with Joab battered the wall, to throw it down.
Then cried a wise woman out of the city, Hear, hear; say, I pray you, unto Joab, Come near hither, that I may speak with thee.
And when he was come near unto her, the woman said, Art thou Joab? And he answered, I am he. Then she said unto him, Hear the words of thine handmaid. And he answered, I do hear.
Then she spake, saying, They were wont to speak in old time, saying, They shall surely ask counsel at Abel: and so they ended the matter.
I am one of them that are peaceable and faithful in Israel: thou seekest to destroy a city and a mother in Israel: why wilt thou swallow up the inheritance of the Lord?
And Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.

The matter is not so: but a man of mount Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, hath lifted up his hand against the king, even against David: deliver him only, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said unto Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to thee over the wall.

Then the woman went unto all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and cast it out to Joab. And he blew a trumpet, and they retired from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem unto the king.
And David said to Abishai, Now shall Sheba the son of Bichri do us more harm than did Absalom: take thou thy lord’s servants, and pursue after him, lest he get him fenced cities, and escape us.
And there went out after him Joab’s men, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men: and they went out of Jerusalem, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.

When they were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa went before them. And Joab’s garment that he had put on was girded unto him, and upon it a girdle with a sword fastened upon his loins in the sheath thereof; and as he went forth it fell out.
And Joab said to Amasa, Art thou in health, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with the right hand to kiss him.

But Amasa took no heed to the sword that was in Joab’s hand: so he smote him therewith in the fifth rib, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and struck him not again; and he died. So Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.
And he went through all the tribes of Israel unto Abel, and to Beth–maachah, and all the Berites: and they were gathered together, and went also after him.

And Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.

Then the woman went unto all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and cast it out to Joab. And he blew a trumpet, and they retired from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem unto the king.

Now Joab was over all the host of Israel: and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites:
And Adoram was over the tribute: and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder:
And Sheva was scribe: and Zadok and Abiathar were the priests:
And Ira also the Jairite was a chief ruler about David.
And David said to Abishai, Now shall Sheba the son of Bichri do us more harm than did Absalom: take thou thy lord’s servants, and pursue after him, lest he get him fenced cities, and escape us.
